record.name: Aged Northern Vietnam Ripe Pu-erh Tea
record.origin: Northern Vietnam highlands, on the Yunnan border, Vietnam

paragraphs.text: This tea comes from the highlands of northern Vietnam, on the border with Yunnan, and was made into [ripe pu’er](shou:definition) the classic way. The leaf was heaped warm and damp in a [fermenting pile](shou:wet-piling) so that heat, moisture and microbes could work through it. It was then left loose rather than pressed, and aged in that form.

brewing.text: Use boiling water, about 7 grams of the loose leaf to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens. Ripe tea forgives a heavy hand and gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, sweet cup with earthy or woody notes. Younger ripe teas can carry a faint smell of the pile, which fades with airing or in the first steeps.
